subject: Re: RFP questions — audit log timestamp provenance & handoff
messages:
From: Anjali Patel <anjali.patel@umbrella-corp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP Q: timestamp provenance and log handoff

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking our RFP — we have a few specific follow-ups related to audit logs and retention that our auditors flagged: 

1) Timestamp provenance: can you describe how timestamps on audit entries are generated (NTP-synced host clocks, monotonic counters, server-side stamping), and whether you can provide evidence that timestamps are untampered (e.g., signed hashes or sequence proofs)?

2) Chain of custody when we request an export: for compliance we need a verifiable handoff that shows the exact slice of logs produced, when the export was generated, and who initiated it. Do you support signed export manifests?

3) Export formats & size: what export formats are available (JSONL/Parquet/etc.), and do you support streaming exports for large volumes? Any documented size limits?

4) Retention policy options: your RFP mentions configurable retention. Please list default retention windows per deployment type and whether retention policies are per-account or per-organization.

We attached Annex A of the RFP for reference. Would appreciate any supporting artifacts you can attach (matrix, sample manifest).

Best,
Anjali
Director, Vendor Compliance
Umbrella Corp

(Attachment: UMB_RFP_Annex_A.pdf)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Anjali Patel <anjali.patel@umbrella-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP Q: timestamp provenance and log handoff

Hi Anjali — thanks for the clear list. Summary answers below; I attached a compact matrix and a short chain-of-custody playbook for your auditors.

1) Timestamp provenance:
- Event stamping: all server-side audit events are stamped with both a monotonic sequence number and an NTP-synchronized UTC timestamp at the point of ingestion. The ingestion tier uses a time-synchronization fleet with stratum-1/2 sources and monitoring to detect drift.
- Tamper evidence: audit shards are maintained in an append-only storage layer. Each shard maintains rolling SHA-256 digests per batch and publishes a daily Merkle root. For Dedicated/Private customers we can supply the per-day Merkle roots and the signed manifest for the requested window.
- Optional signing: for regulated customers we offer export manifests signed with an HSM-backed key (PKCS#11 compatible) to provide non-repudiation. Key rotation policies are available and logged.

2) Chain of custody / export handoff:
- Exports are generated by a signed job that records initiator identity, job id, parameters (time window, filters), and produce-time. The export job produces a manifest.json which includes per-file SHA-256 checksums, row counts, and the Merkle inclusion proof for the shard batch(s) used.
- Delivery: exports can be staged to S3 (customer-owned bucket for Dedicated/Private) or retrieved over a TLS-signed presigned URL for Hosted. We can timestamp the manifest with a vault-signed attestation if required.

3) Export formats & streaming:
- Formats: JSONL (newline-delimited JSON), Apache Parquet, and compressed Avro are supported.
- Streaming: for very large windows we support streaming exports (chunked JSONL) and multipart uploads to S3. We do not impose a hard upper bound on export size for Dedicated/Private—practical constraints are a single export's total object count and per-request throughput; for Hosted we default to 500GB per export job and provide job-splitting guidance.

4) Retention policy options:
- Hosted API: default retention is 90 days for request/response traces and 365 days for index-level telemetry (configurable via contract).
- Dedicated: retention is configurable at the tenancy level; we commonly provision 1yr/3yr options and can do bespoke windows under enterprise agreements.
- Private/on-prem: fully customer-controlled; Redwood ships a retention policy manager that can enforce local deletion and retention tagging.
- Scope: retention is configurable per-account (customer_id) and per-route/pipeline; we can provide retention labels for specific audit streams (security, admin, system).

Attachments: redwood_audit_telemetry_matrix.xlsx, chain_of_custody_playbook.pdf

If helpful, we can schedule a short call to walk through the manifest structure and a sample signed export. I will loop in Marissa (security) and Laura (product) for any parts that need formal attestation.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: redwood_audit_telemetry_matrix.xlsx, chain_of_custody_playbook.pdf)

From: Anjali Patel <anjali.patel@umbrella-corp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP Q: timestamp provenance and log handoff

Evelyn — thanks for the thorough reply. A few quick clarifications from our auditors: 

- When you publish the daily Merkle root, is there a public bulletin or API that we (or an auditor) can query to validate inclusion proofs?
- Does the exported manifest include full request/response payloads by default or are those redacted? We need a mode where full payloads are included for forensic exports (subject to PII controls).
- For the HSM-backed signing, can you confirm the algorithm (e.g., RSA-2048-SHA256 or ECDSA P-256) and whether hardware attestation chains are available to provide to our auditors?

Can we do a 30-minute call on Friday to review a sample manifest? We are in PST.

Best,
Anjali

(Attachment: none)

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP Q: timestamp provenance and log handoff — follow-up & call

Anjali — good questions. Quick answers and proposed attendees for a call: 

- Merkle publication: we host a signed "daily root" API for Dedicated customers and can publish a time-stamped bulletin for Hosted customers on request. Auditors can fetch the root for a date range and validate inclusion proofs using the manifest.
- Payloads in exports: export jobs have a mode toggle: "forensic" (include full request/response payloads, PII redaction disabled) and "compliance" (PII redaction rules applied). Forensic exports require an elevated request with approval logged and are only available under certain contractual controls.
- Signing algorithm: HSM-backed signatures default to ECDSA P-256 + SHA-256; RSA-2048 is available on request. We provide signed certificates and can include attestation certificates from the HSM vendor.

Proposed call: Friday 2027-04-23 at 14:00 PST — I will invite Marissa (head of security) and Laura (product) to answer auditor questions and to review a sample manifest and a short live validation demo. Please confirm or propose another time.

Best,
Evelyn

(Attachment: none)

Hi Anjali — I will join the call and wanted to add a couple of formal items for your auditors ahead of the meeting:

- Mapping doc: we'll provide a short mapping between the RFP control IDs and Redwood's audit event taxonomy (CSV).
- Sample artifacts: a signed manifest, a Merkle root bulletin, and a redacted forensic export example (PII redacted) to demonstrate format and validator steps.
- Attestation: we can furnish a signed attestation of export integrity (on Redwood letterhead) once we complete the sample export validation; typical turnaround is 3 business days.

I will also confirm the available HSM attestation chain for inclusion with the manifest. If there are any specific auditor forms you need completed, please send them and we'll prioritize.

Talk Friday.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
